physical: Interaction with an environment spreads a system's phase relations into degrees of freedom no one can recover, suppressing interference; two branches of a superposition lose coherence faster the more strongly they couple to the environment and the farther apart in position they are.
reflected_sentence: This turns around: holding two outcomes coherent, which the separation made harder, gets easier with receptivity.
rule_reason: one cost with separation_made_by_distance true. Environment coupling does not carry resistance, so the rise with coupling is not a resistance-cost
interpretation: This turns around. What was harder is easier with receptivity. This is not resonance, not Culmination, and not Frequency.
closing: The rule decided. The one cost has separation_made_by_distance true, so the shape turns around. Environment coupling does not carry resistance, so its rise was not a second flip. No variable maps to a frozen word; a rate and an extent do not cross. I did not map the loss of coherence to resonance.
